why: The plan keeps the better of the two pipeline designs (section 8). Both stand at the same levels on all eight profiles, so the choice is in words and is the reader's call. F1 trains the two designs left standing whole, keeps every stage reading scores from fits that did not see the example, runs the leak tests before any card hour and gives every arm a slot. What F2 lacks is not a part of what F1 lacks, nor the reverse; F1's lacks (a tree sample sized to the PC, uncounted disk) can be answered without a card hour, F2's (the designs no longer trained as they stand, heads reading in-sample vectors) cannot.

dropped.reason: It no longer trains either design left standing as it stands, and its heads read the shared reader's vectors on the rows that reader was trained on (D 6.4). What it has that F1 lacks: the four pairings of the two separating decisions at full data, with a prediction for their interaction; trees fitted on all their rows; one reader about 1.7 times larger.
